rule: Call on a receiver of **unknown type**: `recv.member`, using the LAST receiver segment (`self.client.get()` → `client.get`; `a.b.c()` → `b.c`). | Call on a **computed receiver** (call result, index, literal, `super` when the superclass is not in the scan): `.member` — a leading dot means "receiver unknown". | **C4 Unresolved references are preserved.** A call the tool cannot resolve is still emitted as a low guess (`recv.m`, `.m`, a bare name). It is never dropped and never promoted to a resolved ID. | **low**: a guess — receiver of unknown type (`recv.m`, `.m`), or a bare name not found in the scan.
notes: call_type convention used throughout this corpus: a callee that is a member of a type (`T#m`) or a receiver-qualified guess (`recv.m`, `.m`) is `method`; a C function (bare name) is `direct`. This is also the C4 case: none of spin/frobnicate:with:/go/thing is declared anywhere in the scan or by Foundation (the file compiles under manual reference counting, where such sends to `id` are warnings), and each send must still be emitted as a low guess. `id` is the dynamic type, so `[obj m]` → `obj.m` (per-language note). `[s->bar go]`: the field `bar` is declared `id` → unknown receiver, LAST receiver segment `bar.go`. Index `items[0]`, literal `@"abc"` and call result `[obj thing]` are computed receivers → `.member`, low (the literal rule applies even though the literal's class is NSString). Syntax-checked with clang -fno-objc-arc.
